newsitem.title: UK: C.E. Heath jumps after buy-out statement.
newsitem.headline: C.E. Heath jumps after buy-out statement.

text.p: Shares in insurance broker C.E. Heath Plc jumped on Monday, responding to the company's disclosure after Friday's market close of a possible management buy-out.
The stock was up 31-1/2p or 31 percent to 133-1/2 by 0830 GMT.
Heath said on Friday its senior management was in advanced talks about a buyout of the company for just under 100 million stg.
That would value the shares at 143p each, a premium of 63 percent over Friday's opening price of 87.5p, Heath said.

Analysts said on Monday the success of the bid hinged on the funds which have the say in Heath, but added the MBO had a reasonable change to succeed given the poor performance of Heath shares in recent years.
"The MBO sounds to be an entirely appropriate solution", said Charles Landa, insurance analyst at SocGen.
Roman Sizdyn, analyst with Merill Lynch, also said he expected the buyout to go through, adding that it would be the first MBO seen in this sector.
Heath has been turned in the past five years into a medium-sized broker by stripping off its underwriting businesses and demerging its computer services operations.

Heath is controlled by a few investment institutions with fund management group PDFM holding 22 percent of Heath. Both Hambos and Fidelity has a 13 percent stake and Equitable Life has just under five percent.
Mark Powers, head of equities at PDFM, said it was the group's policy not to comment on investment decisions.
